lessons.title: Recognize AI functions
lessons.subtitle: Function, purpose and data over the product name

sections.title: Check functions, not labels
sections.content:
Spam filters, keyboard word prediction, traffic forecasts, image grouping, speech recognition and search ranking can run on machine learning or another AI technique, depending on product and version. A spam filter can also run on fixed rules or statistics. So the product name settles neither the technical nor the legal classification as an AI system.

Record function, version, configuration, purpose, data touched and the responsible unit. What you cannot answer technically stays open until the product owner, the vendor documentation or a technical review settles it.

sections.title: AI functions inside the workday
sections.content:
Document reading, transcription, translation, search, forecasts and assistants can all contain AI-supported functions. Whether one is an AI system under the Regulation depends on how it works and how it is used. The inventory records function and version, purpose, data, users, owner and approval status, so you can assign data rules, review duties and training needs.

Article 4 of the EU AI Act, as it stands, obliges providers and deployers to take measures supporting the development of AI literacy in the people who handle the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf. Technical knowledge, experience, education and training, use context and the people or groups affected all count.

The Article prescribes no inventory, but an inventory shows you the context you are planning for.

quiz.questionText: A colleague uses suggested replies, a transcription function and a route forecast. What can you record with confidence?

answerOptions.text: None of these functions can contain AI techniques
Record all three with version and purpose; check classification
Only the transcription can count as an AI-supported function
Record the functions only after legal classification is finished

quiz.explanation: List function, version, purpose and data first. Whether an entry is an AI system is settled afterwards by technical and legal review.

quiz.questionText: What does Article 4 of the EU AI Act require of providers and deployers?

answerOptions.text: Every company must build its own AI
Every employee must finish a computer science degree
Measures supporting the development of AI literacy in people acting on their behalf
Only IT departments may use AI systems

quiz.explanation: Article 4 requires no degree, own AI or IT monopoly. It requires measures supporting the development of AI literacy in people acting on their behalf, matched to knowledge, experience, use context and the people affected.

sections.title: Compare four operating models
sections.content:
Compare the product edition and how it runs:

| Operating model | Minimum checks | Typical false conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| **Consumer service** | Terms of use, account settings, retention, training use, legal basis, permitted content | Well known or paid for means approved for company data |
| **Enterprise SaaS** | Contract and DPA, roles and permissions, data region, retention, logging, connectors, training use | The enterprise contract covers every configuration and data class |
| **Local or self-hosted** | Model source, device or infrastructure, patches, telemetry, extensions, access, logging | Local means offline, current and safe |
| **Embedded function** | Function and version, activation, data flows, inherited permissions, owner | Approval of the main product covers every new AI function |

Check vendor documents and the contract at procurement, after every material change and at your organization's review triggers.

sections.title: Which tool fits when?
sections.content:
- **Private learning and writing:** A consumer offer can fit if you may share the content and data controls, retention and terms suit the purpose. Use placeholders for other people and never put credentials in a prompt.
- **Work:** Only the product, configuration and workflow approved for this purpose and data class. A business subscription or company account is not yet an approval.
- **Local models:** They can limit data flows. Extensions, telemetry, model downloads, shared machines and missing access controls bring the risk back.

Block 2 covers the full check.

quiz.questionText: You want to draft a private text with an AI assistant. Which statement holds?

answerOptions.text: Only paid business tools are allowed for writing
A consumer offer, if sharing is allowed and data controls, retention and terms fit
No AI tool may be used to write text
Only the best-known product fits, because a brand determines security

quiz.explanation: Private use still depends on content, rights, data controls, retention and terms. Use placeholders for examples and never enter credentials.

quiz.questionText: What separates an approved company workflow from any AI subscription?

answerOptions.text: A company workflow always delivers better answers
Approval covers purpose, data classes, contract, configuration, permissions and responsibilities
A paid subscription may process every data class
Only the provider's EU head office counts

quiz.explanation: An approval covers one purpose, edition, configuration, data class and set of roles. Price, brand and head office check none of that.

lessons.title: Exercise: quick inventory
lessons.subtitle: Ten rows for the functions you really use

sections.title: The AI inventory
sections.content:
For each row note the function, the provider or deployer, the purpose, the data touched and the responsible unit. Whether a function is legally an AI system depends on its version and how it works.

| No. | Product and function | Purpose | Data touched | Approval known? |
|-----|----------------------|---------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Email: suggested replies | | | |
| 2 | Spreadsheet: assistance or pattern detection | | | |
| 3 | Conferencing software: transcription or assistance | | | |
| 4 | Search engine: AI summary | | | |
| 5 | Email: spam filter | | | |
| 6 | Smartphone keyboard: word prediction | | | |
| 7 | Navigation: route or traffic forecast | | | |
| 8 | | | | |
| 9 | | | | |
| 10 | | | | |

Add what you really use in the empty rows. Mark unknowns; product owners, IT or procurement close them.

sections.title: Reading the result
sections.content:
A row is finished when function and version, purpose, data, user roles, owner and approval status are filled in. Unknowns stay marked unknown, because a guess is not an entry. Each open point gets an owner and a next review step.

The result is a working document, neither a full AI register nor complete evidence under Article 4. Article 4 prescribes no inventory format. With the inventory you attach literacy measures, data rules and review routines to the functions in use.

quiz.questionText: A colleague uses suggested replies, a transcription function and a route forecast. What follows for certain?

answerOptions.text: None of the functions can contain AI
Exactly one AI system, because only transcription uses AI
Exactly three standalone AI systems under the AI Act
Record the functions; check classification against product and version

quiz.explanation: A product name does not reveal how many standalone AI systems sit behind it in law. Record function and version, then review.

quiz.questionText: Why does an AI inventory matter?

answerOptions.text: It is needed for the tax return
Without it you cannot judge risks and applicable rules
It is mandatory only for companies from 250 employees upward
It serves IT budget planning and nothing else

quiz.explanation: It is the basis for risk assessment, data rules and responsibilities and supports AI literacy measures. On its own it does not meet the AI Act's requirements.
